reason: Reviewed lifecycle hooks, the Notifai skill, harness setup, CLI readiness and domain terms against the Orca chat change: a device answer to one Codex question card in an Orca chat is now sent through Orca at once, even while another card of the turn is unanswered. None of the five surfaces describes when Orca chat answers are sent or that every card had to be answered first, so none needed a change; hook definitions, the skill, setup, readiness output and domain terms are unchanged. The only new agent-facing text travels inside the delivered answer itself: when another card stays open, the message is Codex's reply envelope naming only the answered card, and its instruction names the other card as still open on the User's devices though Orca's chat no longer shows it, tells the agent not to ask again, and says its answer arrives separately. The acknowledgement context the prompt hook adds is unchanged. A release-authored guidance change note records this for agents. Evidence: focused CLI tests (orca-chat-answers, the hub's Orca chat cases) covering the at-once send, the envelope naming only the answered card, the other card's later answer taking the ordinary route, and the single-card format unchanged; the envelope form itself was proven in a live Orca 1.4.261 chat, where Codex took an envelope naming only one of two cards exactly.
